name: COMP_053
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (82%)** · Ambiguous: Benign vs InSitu · Careful review
InSitu stays in the 90% set; invasive risk is only 1% [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 82%, InSitu 17% | Clear lead |
| Conformal set | Benign, InSitu | Cannot separate them |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.96 / 1.0 | No input concerns |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Benign [F5] | Supports Benign |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 5) · ↓ invasive · Below typical here; pulls away from invasive [F4] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 0, 4, 8) · ↓ invasive · Associated with lower invasive likelihood · Weak
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 2, 3, 6) · ↓ invasive · Duct-confined atypia; lower invasive association · Weak
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 4, 5, 8) · context · Above typical; descriptive only [F2] · Weak
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 3, 6, 10) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; spot check 3/20 · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect versus random is 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007); not shown to reflect the classifier. Unreliable here: necrosis (3/20), normal lobules (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- In situ lesion present: InSitu holds 17% and shares the conformal set.
- Margin tumor call is correct, which 1% invasive risk would miss.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 2, 3** — confirm atypical cells stay within ducts (in situ versus benign).
2. **Region 6** — highest regional invasive risk (39%); look for stromal invasion.
3. **Regions 7, 10, 11** — margins called tumor [F7]; compare with 1% invasive risk.
